hints: Look at the way the three cell symbols are connected round the single loop with the $5.0\text{ }\Omega$ resistor - two drive current one way round the loop and one drives it the opposite way.
Add e.m.f.s acting in the direction of $I$ and subtract the e.m.f. acting against $I$ to find the resultant e.m.f. around the loop.
Use $I = V/R$ with the resultant e.m.f. $V$ and $R = 5.0\text{ }\Omega$, checking that the unit is $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Trace the loop current $I$ past the $3.0\text{ V}$, $4.0\text{ V}$ and $2.0\text{ V}$ cells and note their polarities from the cell symbols.
The $3.0\text{ V}$ and $2.0\text{ V}$ cells act together in one sense round the loop, while the $4.0\text{ V}$ cell is reversed and opposes them.
Apply Kirchhoff's second law for a single loop with negligible internal resistance: resultant e.m.f. = p.d. across resistor.
Calculate resultant e.m.f. $V = 3.0 + 2.0 - 4.0 = 1.0\text{ V}$ in the direction of $I$.
Use $V = IR$ for the $5.0\text{ }\Omega$ resistor: $I = V/R = 1.0/5.0 = 0.20\text{ A}$ with correct unit $\text{A}$.

options.A: Net e.m.f. of $1.0\text{ V}$ across $5.0\text{ }\Omega$ gives $I = 1.0/5.0 = 0.20\text{ A}$.
options.B: Gives $3.0\text{ V}$ net e.m.f., which ignores the opposing $2.0\text{ V}$ cell as well as the $4.0\text{ V}$ cell.
options.C: Gives $5.0\text{ V}$ net e.m.f., which adds $3.0\text{ V}$ and $2.0\text{ V}$ but omits the opposing $4.0\text{ V}$ cell.
options.D: Gives $9.0\text{ V}$ net e.m.f., which adds all three cells $3.0+2.0+4.0$ without allowing for polarity.
